clue.text: Safe from this crime during hours of darkness?

definitions.meaning: reads as being protected from some offence; really the crime is an outrageous overcharge that happens openly
the joke: this crime by its very name happens in broad day, so night is safe from it

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an idiom for blatant overcharging, but read literally it is a theft committed in the day, so nobody suffers it at night.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a blatant swindle or rip-off, which literally means theft done openly while the sun is up.

clue.text: First five ale vats he used for the autumn celebration

indicators.note: the listed letters are put to use in a new order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
V is the Roman numeral for five
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A brewer uses up the first five barrels of beer for a village party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First five' looks like a selection instruction, but First is plain fodder and five is just the Roman V.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the church and community thanksgiving held for the gathered crops each autumn.

clue.text: Princess's bad press etc reflects insolence

parts.note: Di, the familiar name of Princess Diana; the possessive just joins her to what follows

indicators.note: the press and etc are in bad order, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Princess Diana's poor treatment by the newspapers shows their lack of manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing a lack of respect is a synonym for insolent rudeness.

clue.text: Oddly, T-shirt found in back lane entrance

indicators.note: one thing is found inside another, so the selected letters go within the reversed word
the word lane is read back to front

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the odd-numbered letters of T-shirt are kept

parts.note: its first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A strange T-shirt turns up at the entrance to a back alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like a noun for a doorway; it is the verb, stressed on the second syllable, meaning to captivate.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to captivate or spellbind them, the same as holding them spellbound.

clue.text: Geordie goes back to problem

indicators.note: goes back tells the solver to read the dialect word in reverse

parts.note: a Geordie is someone from Newcastle upon Tyne, whose dialect says gan for go, so 'he gans' means he goes

explanation.surface: A man from Newcastle returns to face some difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: Geordie is the nickname for people from Newcastle in north-east England, where 'gan' is the local word for go.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is an unexpected difficulty or hitch, a common synonym for a problem.

clue.text: Push Ann to regret lease of property, reportedly, in a dangerous game

indicators.note: reportedly means the strung-together words are as heard out loud

parts.words: Push Ann to regret lease of property
parts.note: to rush is to push forward hastily; taken as written; to rue is to regret; a let is a lease of a property

explanation.surface: Urging Ann to be sorry for renting out a house, in a risky game.
explanation.walkthrough: RUSH-ANN-RUE-LET said quickly gives the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Russian roulette is a deadly gamble of firing a revolver loaded with one bullet at one's own head.

clue.text: Damn economics and cut a different position for the person next in line

indicators.note: the letters are put into a different position, so they are rearranged
the letter a is cut out of the fodder before the shuffle

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A frustrated economist curses the subject and seeks a new job as heir apparent.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy ranks just below the leader and takes over when that leader is absent.

clue.text: To get a holiday in America I hid in crumpled coat in lorry

indicators.note: the whole assembly sits in the vehicle word, so it goes inside it

parts.note: a van is a small lorry or truck

indicators.note: I is hidden inside the jumbled coat letters
a crumpled coat is out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stowaway hides in a crumpled coat in the back of a truck to reach the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans say vacation where the British say holiday, a period of leisure away from work.

clue.text: Consumption is covered by new support group for sickness

indicators.note: the word for consumption is covered by the group on either side, so it goes inside

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, a famous mutual support group
use is consumption of something

explanation.surface: Someone with tuberculosis joins a fresh self-help group to cope with feeling ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumption' looks like the old name for tuberculosis, a sickness itself, but it simply means use.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is the feeling of wanting to vomit, a kind of sickness or queasiness.

clue.text: Sharp butcher's knife cut out heart

indicators.note: the heart is the middle letter, which is cut out of the knife's name

parts.note: a cleaver is the heavy chopping knife a butcher uses

explanation.surface: A butcher's blade is so keen it could slice out a heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp' looks like it describes the knife, but it is the definition meaning quick-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp person is quick-witted and intelligent, the same as clever.

clue.text: Important to see best bit

parts.note: high as in high-ranking or of great importance
to spot is to see or notice

explanation.surface: It matters to catch the finest part of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the most enjoyable or memorable moment of an event, its highlight.

clue.text: Panda gestation takes a long time

indicators.note: the phrase takes, that is holds, the answer within its letters

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of panda and the start of gestation

explanation.surface: Pregnancy in giant pandas lasts for many months.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, ages means an extremely long while, as in 'I waited for ages'.

clue.text: Greet second fish with rounds of applause

parts.note: a hake is a sea fish of the cod family
to give someone a big hand is to applaud them

explanation.surface: A second catch of fish is welcomed with clapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and shaking someone's palm is a customary way to welcome or greet them.

clue.text: Rider's Oriental journey to find Iran

definitions.note: read as 'Rider is', the definition being the rider; the 's is the link

parts.note: a quest is a long journey in search of something

indicators.note: Iran must be sorted into a new order to find the final letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A horseman sets off eastwards on an expedition to locate Persia.
explanation.definitionFit: An equestrian is a horseback rider, someone skilled at riding horses.

clue.text: Frets, if working gets harder

indicators.note: the letters are working, being reshaped into another word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A guitarist's fingerboard becomes more resistant when it is being played.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiffer means more rigid and less flexible, so firmer or harder.

clue.text: Fruit lost colour in tart

indicators.note: the word for running dye sits in the word for tart

parts.note: curt means brusque or sharp in manner, like a tart reply
a dye that runs loses its colour, so ran

explanation.surface: The fruit in a baked pastry has faded in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' looks like a pastry holding the fruit; it is the adjective meaning sharp-tongued.
explanation.definitionFit: A currant is a small dried grape or a soft berry, both kinds of fruit.

clue.text: Fish Dad cooked in white wine

indicators.note: the cooked letters are placed in the wine's name

parts.note: hock is the British name for German white wine from the Rhine

indicators.note: cooked means altered, so Dad's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Father has prepared fish in a white wine sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Haddock is a North Atlantic sea fish related to cod, popular in fish and chips.

clue.text: Dr Pasteur's solution to rodent infestation?

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
taken as written; solution signals its letters are worked into a new answer

explanation.surface: The famous scientist Pasteur devises a remedy for a plague of rats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solution' does double duty: it signals the scrambled scientist's name and is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring-loaded traps are the standard device for dealing with mice in the house.

clue.text: In contact with posh name after returning work

indicators.note: the name abbreviation comes after the returned work

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U English

indicators.note: the abbreviation for a work is turned back

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone keeps in touch with a fancy figure after coming back to the office.
explanation.definitionFit: Upon means on top of, resting against, so touching or in contact with something.

clue.text: Nowadays, card game is accepted in shortened form

indicators.note: the card game is accepted, taken in, by the date letters

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era
bridge is a card game for four players

explanation.surface: These days a game of cards is permitted in a quicker version.
explanation.definitionFit: An abridged text is cut down or condensed, so it exists in a shortened version.

clue.text: Men taking German's unknown in America

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for German; the possessive just joins it on

indicators.note: the unknown sits in the abbreviation for America

parts.note: y is one of the algebra letters used for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Men carry a German's mysterious object around the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Guys is the informal word for men or fellows, especially in American speech.

clue.text: Chap entered peripheries of French city

indicators.note: the chap entered the edges, going inside them

parts.note: rims are outer edges or peripheries
he is any male person, a chap

explanation.surface: A man made his way to the outskirts of a city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peripheries of French' looks like a request for the outer letters of French, but peripheries is a word in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheims, also spelt Reims, is the cathedral city in Champagne where French kings were crowned.

clue.text: Use an unknown convention

parts.note: to treat someone, well or badly, is to use them
y is a letter used in algebra for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Someone exploits a mysterious gathering of delegates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convention' suggests a conference; here it is a formal agreement between states.
explanation.definitionFit: A convention can be a formal agreement between countries, such as the Geneva Convention, so a pact.

clue.text: Isn't a cog broken by freewheeling?

indicators.note: the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cyclist asks whether a gear tooth snaps when the bike rolls without pedalling.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving along without pedal or engine power, relying on momentum, is coasting.
